fixes.explanation: North it is, baker. The LORD says disaster looms from the north, even great destruction. That's why He says to sound the ram's horn in Tekoa and send up a signal over Beth-haccherem. I think a warning like that is meant to get attention.

A flood is dramatic, friend, and I respect the effort. But this warning doesn't mention water or the sea at all. The LORD says disaster looms from the north, even great destruction. The horn He calls for is about something coming from one direction.

That's the plan, friend. The attackers say, “Rise up, let us attack by night and destroy her fortresses!” They had talked about noon, but now the daylight is fading and the evening shadows grow long (Jeremiah 6:4). So the night becomes their new moment to strike.

Nope, nobody is packing up here. The shepherds are the ones who pitch their tents all around her. Instead of going home, the attackers say, “Rise up, let us attack by night and destroy her fortresses!” Less daylight just changed the schedule.

That's it, baker. The LORD says, “Be forewarned, O Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you; I will make you a desolation, a land without inhabitant.” Notice it starts with a warning. He says it ahead of time, before any of it happens.

That's the word, baker. The speaker says, “Look, their ears are closed, so they cannot hear. See, the word of the LORD has become offensive to them; they find no pleasure in it.” The speaker asks, “To whom can I give this warning? Who will listen to me?” That's a lonely spot to stand in.

Forgotten would be a sad thing, but that's not the word here. The text says, “…the word of the LORD has become offensive to them; they find no pleasure in it.” The word is offensive, and that's the word the text gives.

Confusing is a fair guess, friend, since plenty of things confuse me too, like cabinet instructions. But the text says, “…the word of the LORD has become offensive to them; they find no pleasure in it.” The word is offensive.

That would be a kinder ending, friend, but it's not what the text says. The LORD says, “Their houses will be turned over to others, their fields and wives as well…” The text says the houses go to others, and that's all it says about who gets them.

Deceit is the word, baker. The LORD says, “For from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit.” He names the prophets and priests right alongside everyone else, from the least to the greatest.

That's what they say, friend. The LORD says, “They dress the wound of My people with very little care, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace at all.” It's like saying “it's fine, it's fine” while the oven smokes. The words sound calm, but the LORD says the peace isn't there.

Offerings don't come up in this verse, friend. The LORD says they dress the wound with very little care, “…saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace at all.” The words they say are about peace. It's a calm word on a wound that needs real care.

That's the word, baker. The LORD says, “No, they have no shame at all; they do not even know how to blush.” Blushing is what a face does when it feels ashamed. He says they don't even know how to do that.
